meta.title: A HELOC Isn't a Loan. It's a Credit Card Secured By Your House.
meta.hook: A HELOC works more like a credit line than a one-time loan, and your house secures every dollar drawn.
meta.description: A home equity line of credit (HELOC) and a second mortgage both let you borrow against equity, but they work differently: a second mortgage is one fixed lump sum, a HELOC is a revolving credit line you can draw and repay repeatedly. Both use your home as collateral, which means both carry foreclosure risk if payments are missed. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: A HELOC works more like a credit line than a one-time loan, and your house secures every dollar drawn.

visual.visual_intent: A modest suburban house exterior, warm afternoon light, slow push in
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the house itself as collateral

scenes.narration: Both a home-equity loan and a HELOC let homeowners borrow against equity beyond the first mortgage balance.

visual.visual_intent: Home appraisal papers and house keys laid on a table, natural window light
visual.decision_reason: establishes the shared concept: borrowing against equity

scenes.narration: A home-equity loan usually delivers one lump sum with a set repayment schedule.

visual.query: single stack of cash on table
visual.visual_intent: One neat stack of cash placed once on a table, single deliberate motion, clean light

scenes.narration: A HELOC provides a reusable line during a draw period: borrow, repay, and potentially borrow again.

visual.visual_intent: A card being swiped repeatedly at a counter, implying repeated draw-and-repay use
visual.decision_reason: visual analogy to the credit-card-like revolving structure

scenes.narration: Many HELOCs have variable rates, so required payments can change as benchmark rates move.

visual.query: interest rate percentage sign rising chart
visual.visual_intent: A percentage figure ticking upward on a dark financial display

scenes.narration: The flexibility does not reduce the collateral risk. Failure to repay can lead to foreclosure because the home secures the account.

visual.query: house for sale foreclosure sign yard
visual.visual_intent: A for-sale sign on a house lawn, overcast light, sober documentary tone
visual.decision_reason: the shared collateral risk, plainly stated

scenes.narration: One delivers cash once; the other keeps a credit line open. Both convert home equity into debt.

visual.visual_intent: House keys resting in an open palm, warm closing light, calm final shot
